about: Written by hand: the workspace reorganized by one dependency-injection rule (Sam, msg 1938), as a transformation of the current map. propose.py applies it to map-data.js and writes proposed-data.js; it stops if a trait has no decision, or a move, declaration or adapter names something that is not there. This is a chart for planning, not a change to the code. Where the rule's outcome conflicts with an existing requirement, the proposed graph still shows the rule's outcome and marks it with the conflict, for Sam to decide.
rule: Every trait a crate depends on is a contract, and it is declared by its consumers, not by the crate that implements it.

If a contract is used by more than two crates, it lives in its own contract-only crate (traits, pure value types, and test doubles behind `testing`). Its real implementations move to separate implementation crates that only programs depend on. Model: kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation).
If it is used by two crates or fewer, each consumer declares its own contract, and the program adapts the implementation to it.
Used by: crates other than the definer and the implementers that take the trait in a public slot or call through it, in normal dependencies. Test-only use is listed separately.

conflicts.title: Identify: one identity decision, or one per consumer
conflicts.text: Identify has two consumers, kkt-mcp and kkt-server, so the rule says each declares its own and each program adapts its implementation to both. Step 3 and step 6 made Identify the one place that decides who a caller is, for /mcp, /mcp-admin and the web page alike (step 5's swarm tests rely on all three asking the same Identify). Two contracts allow two answers.

conflicts.title: Real implementations behind `real`, or in implementation crates
conflicts.text: PRINCIPLES rule 8 and CLAUDE.md put what touches the machine in the crate that owns the area, behind its `real` feature (kkt-container's OsHost, kkt-service's OsSystem, ...), and check-crates enforces that only programs turn `real` on. The rule moves each to its own implementation crate, which the program adapts: six new crates, and six adapters in the kkt program.

conflicts.title: Reads and Writes: the store's contract, or the rules'
conflicts.text: Reads and Writes have one consumer, kkt-rules, so the rule has kkt-rules declare them and the programs adapt the store. The plan has a second store (kkt-pro's) implement the same Reads and Writes, with the agreement test and the two-swarm test written over those traits and run against every store, and kkt-store's `testing::swarms_stay_apart` as the check every store must pass. The record types in their signatures would have to move with them, or into a value crate.

conflicts.title: kkt-server's web adapters
conflicts.text: Step 6 made kkt-server's adapters to kkt-web's contract (RulesSource, RulesSources, AdmissionGate) public, for a product that builds its own page, and kkt-server mounts the web page itself. The rule has them stop implementing kkt-web's traits and each program adapt them, so the program, not kkt-server, would hand kkt-web its source and gate.

conflicts.title: Who adapts OperatorWording
conflicts.text: The rule says the program adapts an implementation to its consumer's contract. kkt-format's NoticeWording is wired into the rules by kkt-server, not by a program, and kkt-server must not make decisions: it only wires parts together. Either kkt-server holds the adapter, or the programs pass the wording in.

conflicts.title: The model's own traits fall below the threshold
conflicts.text: Sam names kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation) as the model. Counted by the rule, kkt-db's Backend and Evolve have no consumer besides kkt-db itself, and Connection one (kkt-store). By the count, each would be declared by its consumers and adapted by the program, not shared from a contract crate that the implementation implements. The proposal leaves the model as it is.

assumptions.text: SeededEntropy (repeatable randomness for the web preview and the fake product's differential test, never for tokens) counts as a test double, so it moves into kkt-entropy behind `testing`, not to an implementation crate.
kkt-service's DryRun wraps another System and only prints what it would do; it is the crate's own logic over its contract, not a real implementation, so it stays.
The program kkt counts as a consumer when its code names a trait (for example Box<dyn watch::Server>), as the definition says; kkt-watch::Server's one consumer is the program.
